title: Cinematic AI Video Ads | AIVideosUGC
description: Make cinematic ads from one product photo, with studio-style motion and no crew to book. Describe the scene, then download a tall or wide file and post it.
lead: Make a cinematic ad from the photo you already sell. Describe a scene that would be hard to film, and download it without booking a set.

steps.d: Upload a photo where the product outline is sharp. The move follows that shape.
Name the scene in one line, and name the one fact the clip should say. That line should match the picture.
Put a wide file on the product page and a tall file on a phone feed. The credit cost is shown first.

faq.q: What is a cinematic product video?
faq.a: It is a ready-made open with low light, a slow move, and room for one calm line. You add your photo instead of building a set.

faq.q: How does the template become the clip?
faq.a: You upload the product photo, set the opening line, and pick a voice. You download a wide file or a tall file.

faq.q: Why not book a creator for this open?
faq.a: A creator's calendar decides when the next open exists. Change the spoken line and post the new cut without a crew.

faq.q: Who is a cinematic template for?
faq.a: Shop owners and agencies who need a moody product open. A one-person shop can do it, and so can a team running several products.

faq.q: Can a beginner use this template?
faq.a: Yes. You can walk the three steps with no editing background. A sharp photo of the whole product is enough to start.

faq.q: Which products fit a cinematic open?
faq.a: Any product that should feel like a short film. Each one uses its own photo and the same slow light.

faq.q: May I use photos and clips I already have?
faq.a: Yes. The product in the clip should be the product you ship. A short clip of that same product can join the listing photo.

faq.q: Where can I post the finished open?
faq.a: A tall cut fits TikTok, Reels, and Shorts. A square cut fits a shop grid. A wide cut fits YouTube. You can also download and post it yourself.

faq.q: Do I need a paid plan for this template?
faq.a: Yes. Templates sit on a paid plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. A 15-second video spends 60 credits, shown before the job starts. A failed job returns the credits.

faq.q: Can I use the clip in ads and client work?
faq.a: Yes. Place the clip in a paid ad, on the product page, or in a file you send a client. If a person is on camera, that person is an AI actor.

faq.q: Why start from a template instead of a blank file?
faq.a: The low light and the slow move are already decided. You choose the product in the photo and the one line about it.

steps.sourceAlt: Compact black speaker photographed alone on a dark display stand.
steps.sourceHint: Keep the full product outline sharp against the background.
steps.prompt: A compact black speaker sits on a dark stand by a tall window. One cool highlight hits it as the camera moves closer. The woven front and the rounded outline stay in the center. The last shot still shows the speaker in that light. You hear a quiet room. Add background music if you want it. Keep the speaker's shape, color, and label as in your photo.
steps.resultAlt: Rounded pebble-shaped black speaker catches a cool cinematic highlight on a dark sideboard.

definition.title: What Is a Cinematic Ad?
paras: A cinematic ad is a slow open on one product photo, with the light kept low, so the product arrives before the sales line.
You choose the sentence, and whether a music track sits under the scene. A wide file goes to the product page. A tall file goes to a phone feed.

reasons.h2: Full Control of the Cinematic Ad
reasons.lead: You get the tools for a studio-style ad, and you do not need a production background.

items.d: Describe a scene that would be too hard or too costly to shoot. The clip starts from the photo you already have.
Say the line in the language on the product page. The same scene stays, and the captions follow.

items.t: A Ready Scene, Not a Blank File
items.d: Start from a scene that already has a light and a move. You bring the photo and the one line.
Trim, cut, and polish the clip in the editor. You do not switch to another tool for that pass.
A short line can sit on the move, and you can reposition it before you export.
Save a TikTok cut, an Instagram cut, a Facebook cut, or a YouTube file. Download it and post it yourself if you prefer.

more_sections.h2: What You Can Add to a Cinematic Ad
more_sections.lead: A calm line and a music bed can ride under the open, so the ad is finished from one photo.

items.d: Use a ready-made voice, or a clone from a short sample you have rights to, so you are not booking a voice actor.
A short line can sit on the move, and you can reposition it in the editor before export.
The same setup can cover the products you sell, so one light serves the whole line.
Paste a product page and the move uses the product shown there.

items.t: A Spoken Line You Can Edit
items.d: A draft line about the product can be written for you, and you can edit it before the voice reads.

items.t: An AI Actor in the Open
items.d: An AI actor can appear when a person should be on camera. Keep the product alone in frame when the object should lead.
Music from the library can sit under the scene, or the scene can carry the voice alone.
You can trim the move so the product is named once it fills the frame, with the caption beside it.
Run the same shot in the language you sell in. You switch the spoken line and the captions, with no new shoot.
The open can go to YouTube, Facebook, or Instagram from the account you connect. Downloading and posting yourself is there too.
Your shop software can send each product photo in, so a whole line can use the same open.

more_sections.h2: Full Creative Control From One Photo
more_sections.lead: You set the scene, the spoken line, and the frame size. The product photo is the only thing you need to bring.

items.d: Put the product in the scene you describe. It comes from the photo you already have, so there is no set to rent.
Speak the line in the language on the product page. The same slow move stays, and the captions follow.
The slow move and the low light are already in the template. You bring the photo and the one line you want heard.
Trim the move, shift the caption, and swap the track in the editor. A wording fix does not start a new crew call.
Captions land with the spoken line. You read them and fix a wrong word before the file goes out.
Export wide for the product page, or tall for a phone feed. The same photo covers both cuts.
